summary: Annette Schmiedchen is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Humboldt University of Berlin (~1989–1994) and her Habilitation from Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (2008), later holding positions at both institutions.

Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1969), where he taught from circa 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~2001–2007) and became Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison circa 2012.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a Sinologist and historian. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928, later serving there as a lecturer (1946) and succeeding Duyvendak as Professor of Chinese (1956–1975).

Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctorate under John Brough at SOAS (~1949–1954), subsequently holding posts at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol and a DPhil at the University of Oxford (1995) supervised by Alexis Sanderson, later teaching at the University of Montana.
Anthony W. Barber specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 and held a post at the University of Calgary, attested in 1998.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Paris, EPHE, and Sorbonne under Ferdinand de Saussure, later holding professorships at INALCO (1902–1906) and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as professor at INALCO and Collège de France (1806–1838), rector of the University of Paris (1815), and president of the Société Asiatique.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, taught Persian at INALCO, and held the Sanskrit chair at Collège de France (1815–1832).

Anton Boller was an Austrian scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as a lecturer and extraordinary professor at the University of Vienna before becoming Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Sanskrit there in 1855.
Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his Dr. phil. at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1831) and later served there as a Dozent from 1849 to 1852.

Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at the Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy and the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

Anton Westermann was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his habilitation at Leipzig University (1825–1830), where he subsequently served as co-director from 1830 to 1865.
Antonino Forte was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1982–1999) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1989–2006).

Antonio T. de Nicolás was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. After earning his PhD from Fordham University, he served as a professor of philosophy at Stony Brook University from circa 1969 to 1996.

Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University in 2010 under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and later served as scholar in residence at BDRC.
Anuj Misra is a scholar who studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker from circa 2013 to 2016.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, later serving as an assistant lecturer there (attested 1943) and director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

Arata Okayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto, Tokyo, and Peking universities, and held professorships at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia and the University of Tokyo (1995–2012).
